result.note: Tests the new partnership level, the trade and payments outcomes, and the maritime and defence commitments from To Lam's May 2026 India visit.

questions.prompt: In May 2026, during the India visit of Vietnamese President To Lam, India–Vietnam bilateral ties were elevated to which level?
questions.explain: The visit concluded on 7 May 2026 with ties raised to an Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. TBB reads the upgrade as part of a middle-power effort to stay insulated from US-China friction.
questions.source: President To Lam of Vietnam wrapped up his India visit today, elevating bilateral ties to an Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to insulate both nations from superpower friction.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the economic outcomes of the India–Vietnam summit held in May 2026:
items: The two countries set a bilateral trade target of USD 25 billion by 2030.
India's UPI is to be linked with Vietnam's Fast Payment System.
The two sides pledged to complete the review of the ASEAN India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) by the end of 2028.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the leaders pledged to finish the AITIGA review by year-end, meaning the end of 2026, to fix trade imbalances. A critical minerals pact and the UPI linkage are central to reaching the USD 25 billion goal.
questions.source: They also pledged to finish the ASEAN India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) review by year-end to fix trade imbalances.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Vietnam maritime and defence commitments made in May 2026:
items: The two countries committed to expanding oil and gas exploration in accordance with international law.
Defence cooperation will include regular joint hydrographic surveys and increased naval port calls.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both commitments were made. The reference to international law on oil and gas exploration is read as a nod to resisting Beijing's maritime claims in the South China Sea, and the two sides also agreed to move beyond buyer-seller roles to co-produce military technology.
questions.source: This includes regular joint hydrographic surveys and increased naval port calls to boost maritime awareness.
